key_insight: The paper connects data-driven and theoretical turbulence closures for stratified ocean flows, aiming to better represent unresolved mesoscale eddies in coarse-resolution models.
engineering_relevance: Improved closure models can make ocean simulations more accurate and computationally feasible for predicting momentum, energy, and tracer transport.
method: Compare theoretical and AI/data-driven mesoscale closure formulations
Use analytical and data-driven methods to identify relationships between closure approaches
Target stratified, rotating, Boussinesq ocean dynamics with subgrid-scale effects
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates the authors examine a range of theoretical and data-driven closures and analyze their connections, rather than presenting a single standalone benchmark.
watch_item: Bridging theory and ML may improve interpretability, but closure performance and generalization can depend strongly on flow regime and training data coverage.
paper_title: Towards bridging the gap between data-driven and theoretical turbulence closures in stratified flows
